svg.title: Step 2 · How a question's answer streams
svg.desc: The chat page's form posts the question to /api/chat with htmx. The chat route reads and checks the form: a broken rule gets our own sentence, with its status. Otherwise the answer streams back as server-sent events of HTML: first the question and Nimbus's empty, busy answer, which htmx adds to the conversation; then a piece per word, each added to that answer; then the finished answer in its place. Stop aborts the request, and the server, hearing the browser go, ends the stream and logs it as aborted; a failure shows the answer so far, our own sentence and its ref. Each step writes a log line.
svg.text: Step 2 · How a question's answer streams
From the form to each word on your screen, and Stop
Your browser: the chat page
the form: htmx 4's hx-post
hx-sync this:drop: one at a time
chat.js: Stop, our own sentences
POST
nimbus/chat.py: chat(), POST /api/chat
read_chat_request(): a form · at most 32 KiB · each field once
ChatRequest: the question, trimmed, 1 to 2,000 characters
a broken rule: 400, 413 or 415, our sentence, x-nimbus-error
stream_turn(): the answer, as server-sent events of HTML, in an EventStream
① The turn
your question, and Nimbus's
answer, empty and aria-busy
htmx adds both to the end
of #messages (beforeend)
② A piece per word
answer.py: the fixed answer,
a word every 60 ms
each an hx-partial, added to
the end of #answer-ID
③ The end
the finished answer, no
longer busy, in the place of
#turn-ID (outerHTML)
then chat.done is logged
text/event-stream · no-store · however it ends, its source is closed within the request, so
the answer's last line comes before the request's own; a browser that has gone isn't an error
④ Stop
chat.js: htmx:abort, and the browser drops the stream
the server hears it go and cancels the stream
chat.aborted, never an error · the page: "Stopped."
⑤ A failure
the answer so far, then our own sentence and its
ref, the end of the request's id: "(ref 33a7af21)"
chat.failed: the error's class, never its text
The logs: chat.request (the question's length, never its text) · chat.done, aborted or failed · http.request
The server makes every event's HTML, every value escaped; htmx puts it in place.
Our own script only ever adds text, and no script is inline: the policy still allows only our files.
